title: Canonical-path effective-resistance lower bound for intrinsic kinetic rows
question: Can a deterministic canonical-path load bound give a valid finite lower envelope for the intrinsic momentum graph, while exposing the exact conductance and probability inputs needed for a uniform proof?

new_perspective.principle: Replace an eigenvalue-only finite stress by a constructive path certificate: a spanning tree and its effective-resistance load produce an explicit Poincare lower bound that can be audited edge by edge.
route: For every conditional law pi, form the symmetric momentum conductance c_ij=(pi_i+pi_j)|p_ij|^2/(2 chi) and choose a deterministic maximum-conductance spanning tree.
For each unordered pair x<y, route the pair mass pi_x*pi_y along its unique tree path gamma_xy and compute load(e)=sum pi_x*pi_y*len(gamma_xy) over paths containing e.
Set rho=max_e load(e)/c_e. The finite canonical-path inequality Var_pi(f)<=rho E(f) yields the constructive lower bound rho^(-1) for every likelihood row.

Compare rho^(-1) with the exact intrinsic generalized gap, record minimum tree conductance, path length, conditional probability floor and tree-choice profiles, and repeat the full R-404 source/history/orientation grid.

Use a factor-of-two path inequality mutation, a q-for-p conductance mutation and a disconnected toy graph in the hostile lane; these make normalization, generator support and connectivity load-bearing rather than decorative.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A promoted route would require a cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform family of paths or a geometric flow decomposition with rho bounded, together with an invariant common-core identification of the momentum form. The finite certificate supplies the exact analytic debt but is not itself a QFT gap theorem.

finite_theorem.conductance: c_ij=(pi_i+pi_j)|p_ij|^2/(2 chi), with symmetric graph energy E(f)=sum_{i<j} c_ij(f_i-f_j)^2
finite_theorem.finite_bound: Var_pi(f)<=rho E(f), hence E(f)>=rho^(-1)Var_pi(f) for every finite f
finite_theorem.tree_choice: Any connected spanning tree is valid; maximum-conductance Kruskal is only a deterministic finite certificate and is not assumed uniformly stable
finite_theorem.normalization: The pair sum is over unordered x<y, so no extra factor 2 enters the bound; a doubled bound is hostile-tested as invalid.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar nonnegativity and the unordered-pair path bookkeeping skeleton; conductance matrices, tree construction, Gibbs rows, spectra and all uniform/QFT limits remain in the executable/open boundary.

promotion_criteria: Construct a cutoff-independent path or flow family on a Hamiltonian common core with rho bounded above and tree-edge conductances bounded below in the required weighted sense.
Control source, phase, volume, orientation and exhaustion dependence, including cross-phase paths and neutral-sector mass.
Identify the canonical-path lower bound with the R-399 shell and then discharge common-core/common-alpha and OS/KMS/GNS gates before any physical mass-gap language.
stop_conditions: If rho grows without a proved compensating normalization or the bound collapses under cutoff/volume stress, retain the route as a finite diagnostic and do not substitute it into the shell proof.
If a graph loses connectivity, a probability or conductance floor fails, or the path residual becomes negative, stop the finite lane and record the exact obstruction.
If path normalization or tree choice is treated as a hidden constant, reject the route; finite positivity is not a uniform or QFT theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite canonical-path/effective-resistance checkpoint only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform gap, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The path certificate is a constructive finite lower bound and a list of uniformity inputs. It does not turn the observed finite envelope into an analytic regulator or thermodynamic estimate.
